newsitem.title: UK: Ship losses fall in Q4 1996 -UK insurance body.
newsitem.headline: Ship losses fall in Q4 1996 -UK insurance body.

text.p: The number of merchant ships lost in the final quarter of 1996 improved, but losses for the year as a whole were up on 1995, The Institute of London Underwriters (ILU) said.
One hundred and five ships over 500 gross tonnes (gt) were lost last year, compared with 95 in 1995. However, the tonnage lost declined to 653,775 from 693,433, the ILU said in a statement.
"After the exceptional improvement in 1995, these figures demonstrate a return to a more normal loss pattern last year."
The ILU noted that the 1996 figures will rise as confirmation of major casualties filters through.
Bulk carriers dominated the loss statistics in the final quarter, including the 36,120 gt Bright Field, which crashed into New Orleans dockside.
The year was notable for the number of accidents involving cruise liners and ferries, the ILU said, adding that it will publish full 1996 statistics on January 28.
